sub_claims.statement: s > 5/2 is the classical local well-posedness threshold for the Einstein vacuum Cauchy problem on asymptotically flat data (nabla g, k in H^{s-1}).
sub_claims.evidence_quality: preprint; the statement attributes the result to [H-K-M], which was not fetched

sub_claims.statement: h - delta_ij = O(r^-1) and K = O(r^-2) is the standard asymptotically flat decay family.
sub_claims.evidence: LR2005 Section 1: metric o(r^{-1-sigma}), K o(r^{-2-sigma}), sigma > 0 (peer-reviewed); CK's strongly AF class o(r^{-3/2}), o(r^{-5/2}) quoted in the same footnote
sub_claims.evidence_quality: peer-reviewed; rates are strictly faster than the schema's big-O rates and derivative counts are not enumerated

sub_claims.statement: The weighted normalization h - delta_ij in H^s_delta, K in H^{s-1}_{delta+1} is the standard published form.
sub_claims.evidence: ABSENT in all four checked sources; BI2004 Section 3 uses a different convention: (g-ring + H^2_{-1/2}) x H^1_{-3/2} (negative decay indices, momentum more negative); BIERI2009 uses interior/exterior weighted L^p norms
sub_claims.evidence_quality: absence in a bounded checked set + positive evidence of different conventions; not a proof that no source states the schema's form
sub_claims.schema_field: spaces: "h - delta_ij in H^s_delta, K in H^{s-1}_{delta+1}"

sub_claims.statement: The upper endpoint 1 of the interval delta in (1/2, 1) is part of the standard statement.
sub_claims.evidence: no checked source states a delta-range at all
sub_claims.evidence_quality: absence in a bounded checked set

schema_status_recommendation.reason: SC3 and SC4 (the weighted encoding and the delta interval) have no locator in the checked open set; clearing the flag would promote fluent text to a verified citation
schema_status_recommendation.permitted_upgrade: add the KR2001 Theorem 1.1 / Remark 1.2 locator for the s > 5/2 threshold and the LR2005 Section 1 locator for the AF decay family as PARTIAL support annotations
schema_status_recommendation.required_from_owner: a section/page locator in a named source for the exact H^s_delta / H^{s-1}_{delta+1} normalization and the delta in (1/2,1) interval (the schemas' provenance names only 'Choquet-Bruhat-Geroch maximal development' with identifier null, which does not cover this field)
schema_status_recommendation.convention_hazard: weight indices appear with opposite signs across the literature (BI2004: H^2_{-1/2} x H^1_{-3/2}); the schema uses positive delta and delta+1, so any borrowed locator must be checked for index-sign convention before it is bound

decision_rule.SC1: SUPPORTED iff all KR quote patterns present; else NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SET
decision_rule.SC2: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED iff all LR quote patterns present (rates are little-o and faster than the schema's big-O, derivative counts absent); else NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SET
decision_rule.SC3: NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SET iff the exact normalization is absent from every checked source AND a different convention is positively attested; else UNRESOLVED
decision_rule.SC4: NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SET iff the interval is absent from every checked source; else UNRESOLVED
decision_rule.overall: SUPPORTED only if SC3 and SC4 are both SUPPORTED; otherwise PARTIAL; CHECK_FAILED if any integrity/quote/control check fails

falsifier: A fetched primary source with an exact locator (section, theorem or page) that states the schema's conjunction: h - delta_ij in H^s_delta and K in H^{s-1}_{delta+1} with s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2, 1), on asymptotically flat vacuum data. Such a source flips SC3/SC4 and the overall verdict to SUPPORTED.
next_falsifier: A source showing delta > 1/2 alone (no upper endpoint) is the standard statement, which would make the schema's '(1/2, 1)' interval an unlicensed strengthening; or a source showing the standard threshold for the weighted class is not s > 5/2.
non_claims: Does not assert that the schema's normalization is wrong or non-standard; only that it was not found in the four checked open sources.
Does not clear the UNVERIFIED flag and does not resolve any G-FORM gate item.
